summary: Gable-roof L-4 cab built in 1931 on Oregon Butte in the Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness; staffed in summers, reached only by trail, and reported saved in the 2021 Green Ridge fire.

access.note: Reached on foot or horseback on Forest Service Trail #3134 in the Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness; the cab is a staffed lookout.

visit.trail_note: About three miles from the Teepee Trailhead, crossing a ridge and a saddle.

events.note: Site established, per TrailChick; the current structure dates from 1931
Gable-roof L-4 cab; the register, firelookout and TrailChick agree
Spike Armstrong named as the lookout in an August 1953 Umatilla National Forest News item, as quoted on a third-party site
Register: restored in 1980 and regularly staffed since
Green Ridge fire, July 2021; cab reported saved by fire wrap and retardant drops (single source)

evidence.supports: high point of SE Washington's Blue Mountains
evidence.quote: Oregon Butte is the highest point in southeastern Washington and the Washington side of the Blue Mountains.
Built in 1931, Oregon Butte Lookout on the Umatilla National Forest in southeastern Washington is one of them.
Accessible only by trail, it is located within the Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness and was in active status until 1972.

evidence.supports: 200 gable-roof L-4 lookouts pre-1933; fewer than 15 remain
evidence.quote: At one time there were 200 gable-roof L-4 lookouts throughout the Northwest (pre-1933), and now fewer than 15 remain.
Built in 1931, this gable-roof L-4 cab is staffed every summer.
The gable-roofed L-4 fire lookout atop Oregon Butte was built in 1931 and is staffed every summer by a veteran fire lookout.
Site Established: 1914
Current Structure Built: 1931
January 15, 1996
Spike Armstrong has a lookout on Oregon Butte who has made an ingenious pack saddle for his big dog Shadrack.
The dog packs water and groceries to the lookout.
In 1980 the structure was restored and has since been regularly staffed.
Lightning strikes on July 7, 2021 ignited both the Turkey Tail and Green Ridge fires, which were managed as one fire, the Green Ridge fire.

evidence.supports: over 40,000 acres; evacuation of Oregon Butte
evidence.quote: The fire burned over 40,000 acres in the Blue Mountains causing the evacuation of Oregon Butte.

evidence.supports: lookout saved by fire wrap and retardant drops
evidence.quote: The fire eventually burned over the Butte but the lookout was saved thanks to protective fire wrap and retardant drops from aerial support.
Trees within 100 yards of the lookout were damaged in the fire.

evidence.supports: trail from Teepee Trailhead to the lookout
evidence.quote: This trail begins at Teepee Trailhead and ends at Oregon Butte.

evidence.supports: trail maintained for foot and horse use only
evidence.quote: It is maintained for foot and horse use only, since it is located within the Wenaha-Tucannon Wilderness.

evidence.supports: three-mile trail crossing ridge and saddle
evidence.quote: Within its three mile length, this trail climbs and descends across a ridge and through a saddle toward Oregon Butte.

evidence.supports: staffed each year by Pomeroy Ranger District
evidence.quote: The lookout is actively staffed each year by the Pomeroy Ranger District.
Looks in good shape, no problems, in pretty remarkable shape

notes_for_editor: The 2021 Green Ridge fire account (lookout saved by fire wrap and retardant drops) rests on one blog, TrailChick; check against Forest Service fire reports. The 1914 site date also comes only from TrailChick. The 1953 anecdote is quoted on a third-party site from a Umatilla National Forest News item dated August 14, 1953; the original was not read. The register says active status until 1972 and restoration in 1980; the gap is not explained by any source read. Record access was 'unknown'; facts.access is set to public (trail access, staffed cab) from the Forest Service trail page. No rental information found. Record checks out: elevation 1946.8 m matches the register's 1,947 m, and the coordinates match the register.
